angles.drive: You see the whole answer first and work out the steps after. You need the shape of a thing before its parts, so you trust what you saw rather than what you can prove. Take the whole picture seriously and let the proof catch up.
angles.cost_self: Seeing it whole is how you know a thing is true. Because you want proof to show, you sit on the picture rather than use it. If you act on what you see early, you keep the head start that waiting throws away.
angles.cost_others: Explaining a thing, you give the whole picture and skip the path. You care about the ending more than the steps, and hand over the answer without the way to it. Walk one person through it slowly, and you leave them the path too.

angles.drive: Most of what you know, you taught yourself. You own a thing only once you work it out alone, so you would rather find your own way than take a course. Teach yourself the dull basics too, to keep your knowledge free of holes.
angles.cost_self: Self-taught is the only learning you trust. Because a thing has to be found before it feels true, you spend months finding it alone rather than an hour being told. Whenever a lesson would spare you the search, take it and keep those months.
angles.cost_others: You turn down help with anything you are learning. Being self-taught matters more to you than being shown, and you never let a friend who knows it well share it. Say yes to one lesson as a kindness to the person who offers it.

angles.drive: Your best thinking happens with nobody else in it. You need quiet to hear your own thinking, so you take a question away to think it through rather than talk it out. Set that quiet aside before you have to think in a crowd.
angles.cost_self: When something weighs on you, you think it through alone first. Because talking before you have an answer feels unsafe, you carry the worry alone rather than share it. Let one person into your thinking to get the comfort you now go without.
angles.cost_others: Working something out, you go quiet on everyone around you. Because you think best alone rather than with others, you leave the people beside you on their own. When you need to think, say it first and stay close enough to be good company.

angles.drive: One idea at a time gets the whole of you. You feel awake only inside one subject, so you follow it all the way down instead of keeping the rest of the week going. Keep in mind that your life waits where you left it.
angles.cost_self: One subject at a time is how you take things in. You give it the hours meant for sleep rather than a stopping point, since you feel awake nowhere else. Do not forget that the rest you skip never comes back as insight.
angles.cost_others: When one idea has you, you are reachable only through it. Because you steer every talk back onto its track rather than let it change, you leave family and friends outside. You give them only the part of you that talks about it.

angles.drive: You give a new interest everything or nothing at all. You count half an effort as none, so you give a thing every hour rather than a steady few until the wanting runs out. After the push, you go weeks without touching it at all.
angles.cost_self: All or nothing is the only speed you have. Since you never learn at half speed, you give a subject one hard month rather than a slow year, and the month ends first. You stop at half the skill, right where the feeling did.
angles.cost_others: Starting something together, you give it all of you until the switch goes off. You pull a friend in at full strength rather than a pace that lasts, so the plan outlives your part. Remember as well that you leave someone holding what you started.

angles.drive: You hold your inner life in, even with the people you trust. Because words feel too small for what goes on in you, you hold it all in rather than explain it. Whatever you hold in, you carry by yourself for longer.
angles.cost_self: Whenever something matters, you hold it in a little longer. You would rather keep a thought safe than say it badly, and you give the people near you the tidy version. Held back like this, you lose the closeness of being known half finished.
angles.cost_others: Most troubles you hold in until you have handled them. Since a struggle feels safer unspoken, you give your family the outcome rather than the story. Each time you do, you take from them the chance to stand beside you through it.

angles.drive: You see finished things where others see empty air. The business before the market exists, the picture before the first stroke, the version of a person they have not met yet. The visions arrive lit from inside, complete, and your job is mostly transcription.
angles.cost_self: You described the neighborhood’s future to a skeptical friend in 2019, cafe by cafe, almost address by address. You were renting there anyway when the wave arrived. The friend brings up that walk every time property prices come up, in the tone people use for eclipses.
angles.cost_others: People dismiss your predictions at intake and quote them at parties three years later. The pattern has repeated enough that a few colleagues now write down your stray remarks, timestamped, as a hobby. Their notebook, they say, outperforms their financial advisor. They are not entirely joking.

angles.drive: Your mind switches on when the world switches off. After eleven, the connections arrive: the insight, the fix, the strange idea with the workable center. Daylight-you executes what midnight-you discovers, a two-shift operation everyone mistakes for one ordinary person.
angles.cost_self: The solution to the storage problem arrived at 1:40am, complete, while the house slept, and you built the prototype by breakfast using a lamp and a towel to muffle the drill. The team spent Tuesday marveling. You spent Tuesday napping, having already been to Wednesday.
angles.cost_others: People learn to check their messages in the morning for your timestamps: 12:51, 2:14, 3:03, each carrying something the daylight meetings could not produce. Employers have stopped policing your hours. Whatever happens in your small hours arrives at standup already glowing, and nobody audits a lighthouse.

angles.drive: Your knowing arrives without visible sources. The diagnosis before the tests, the reading of a stranger at a glance, the sense that this flight, this deal, this person is wrong. Asked to explain, you produce nothing auditable. Asked to be right, you mostly are.
angles.cost_self: You told your friend not to take the apartment, unable to name a single concrete reason beyond the light felt wrong. She took it. The mold survey, the neighbor situation, and the landlord’s lawsuit all surfaced within the year, in roughly the order your discomfort had.
angles.cost_others: People consult you off the record, slightly embarrassed, the way executives consult weather folklore before big launches. Your hit rate embarrasses them further. Nobody builds a slide around your feelings, and increasingly nobody signs anything big without, casually, asking what your gut says first.

angles.drive: One idea takes the whole house. The new interest arrives like ignition: gear bought, sleep skipped, meals forgotten, conversation rerouted through the topic for weeks. The heat is genuine and total, and everything else in your life stands in its light, waiting, unwatered.
angles.cost_self: The chess phase lasted seven weeks and consumed roughly two hundred hours, four apps, one physical clock, and every anecdote you told. Then, on an unremarkable Thursday, it simply stopped burning. The board is under the bed now, with the telescope, the loom, and the kanji cards.
angles.cost_others: Your people track your obsessions like weather systems: naming them, estimating duration, planning around the blast radius. They have learned not to invest in the current one and not to mention the last one. What they miss, quietly, is the version of you between fires. He rarely visits.

angles.drive: Your energy arrives on a schedule no one, including you, can publish. Tuesday-you rewires the kitchen at midnight and Thursday-you cannot answer a text. Plans made in a bright phase get inherited by a dim one, and both phases sign your name with equal authority.
angles.cost_self: You committed to the weekend workshop during Monday’s blaze, prepaid and enthusiastic, and arrived at Saturday as a different person, one who sat in the parking lot for forty minutes and drove home. The refund window had closed. The pattern, your partner noted, has a subscription.
angles.cost_others: People quote two versions of you and specify which one they mean: bright-you and gone-you. Invitations come with soft confirmations layered in, checked twice, once at acceptance and once the night before. Nobody calls it unreliability to your face. The scheduling apparatus around you says it hourly.

angles.drive: Your inner world drifted from the shared one by degrees. The interests nobody around you shares, the hours nobody keeps, the references that land on silence: each pulled you a little further offshore. People love you from the mainland. The commute between you has gotten long.
angles.cost_self: At the reunion you spent the evening at the edge of three conversations, fluent in none of them, holding your drink like a permission slip. The people were kind and the kindness had distance in it. You left early, relieved, and the relief troubled you the whole drive home.
angles.cost_others: Old friends describe you now with the phrase in their own world, said warmly and with a small shrug. Invitations still come, at holidays, in the plural, addressed to a version of you they remember. The estrangement was nobody’s decision. It accumulated, like heat leaving a house.
